classification.difficultyReason: Convert each target date into years since 2011, then substitute into the supplied population model and interpret the result as a population estimate.

content.prompt: On 1 January 2011, the population of the world was estimated to be $7\,074\,000\,000=7.074\times10^9=A$. Assume that the population of the world is increasing at the rate of $3\%$ per year, so that $N=A(1.03)^t$ after $t$ years.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Estimate what the population of the world will be on 1 January 2016. Give your answer in scientific notation to 5 significant figures.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}t&=2016-2011\\t&=5\\N&=7.074\times10^9(1.03)^5\\N&\approx8.2007\times10^9\end{align*}$$The estimated population is $8.2007\times10^9$ people, to 5 significant figures.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Estimate the population on 1 January 2111. Give your answer in scientific notation to 4 significant figures.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}t&=2111-2011\\t&=100\\N&=7.074\times10^9(1.03)^{100}\\N&\approx1.360\times10^{11}\end{align*}$$The estimated population is $1.360\times10^{11}$ people, to 4 significant figures.
